findings.title: Null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty in the Meet fallback
Google update and delete calendar lookup is circular and always undefined
Google createEvent organizer email and calendar selection ignore the credential
Collective team destination calendars can be duplicated or mutated, and pushed onto null
Dynamic group users no longer select the organization
Unhandled missing credential on update, and unfiltered DB fetch of arbitrary credentials
Event result externalId is only set for the credential-based path

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty in the Meet fallback

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-121

Explanation:
`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError whenever the location is Google Meet and no destination calendar exists. The old code used `?.`, so this is a regression.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar") {
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Google update and delete calendar lookup is circular and always undefined

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-257
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:312-318

Explanation:
In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy. The code then runs `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, which compares against that falsy value and never matches a real calendar. The fallback therefore always yields undefined, whereas before it used `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates and deletes without an explicit external id lose their target calendar.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ?? event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId;
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Google createEvent organizer email and calendar selection ignore the credential

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100-103
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145-154

Explanation:
The organizer email is always taken from the first destination calendar, even when the event is being created on another host's credential. When the credential matches no destination calendar, the event falls back to "primary". That is acceptable, but createEvent also now requires `credentialId`, and other callers or tests may not pass it. `EventManager` also passes `destination.externalId` to `createEvent`, but Google ignores it and re-derives the calendar by credentialId. If one credential has several destination calendars, this picks the wrong one.

Proposed fix:
Select the destination calendar by credentialId for the organizer email as well, and pass the explicit externalId through to the service.

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Collective team destination calendars can be duplicated or mutated, and pushed onto null

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987-1006
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1079

Explanation:
`teamDestinationCalendars` is filled inside async `map` callbacks. This works only because the pushes happen synchronously before the first await, which is fragile. `evt.destinationCalendar` can also be `null` (neither eventType nor organizer has one), so the optional-chained `push` silently drops the team calendars. Also, `eventType.destinationCalendar` is a single calendar for the whole event type, so team members' calendars are added alongside it.

Proposed fix:
Build the array explicitly, and initialize `destinationCalendar` as `[]` rather than `null`. Collect the team calendars synchronously with a plain loop.

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Dynamic group users no longer select the organization

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:731-742

Explanation:
The `organization: { select: { slug } }` selection was removed from the dynamic user query. Downstream code that reads `user.organization` may break or lose data. The refactored `loadUsers` also now throws for an empty `dynamicUserList`, and wraps every other error as a 500, which hides the original error.

Proposed fix:
Restore the `organization` select and avoid the broad catch-and-rethrow.

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Unhandled missing credential on update, and unfiltered DB fetch of arbitrary credentials

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:511-542
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:431-441

Explanation:
If the credential is not found in memory or in the DB, `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential. The DB lookup by id has no ownership check, and the extra queries run inside loops. In the cancel handler, the recurring-event branch inside the per-reference loop deletes all remaining bookings once per calendar reference, which duplicates the deletes.

Proposed fix:
Skip references with no resolvable credential. Verify credential ownership. Move the recurring deletion outside the reference loop.

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Event result externalId is only set for the credential-based path

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:376-381
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:169-170

Explanation:
In the `else` branch, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without an externalId. The stored reference then has `externalCalendarId` undefined. Booking references created through that path lose their calendar id, which affects later updates and deletes.

Proposed fix:
Pass `destination.externalId` in that branch as well.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty in the Meet fallback - destructuring yields undefined when array is empty or null, then reading .integration without optional chaining throws TypeError
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: when destructuring mainHostDestinationCalendar from evt.destinationCalendar, if destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar becomes undefined. The golden comment mentions this happens in createEvent() and updateEvent(), while the candidate specifically mentions the 'Meet fallback' context where .integration is accessed without optional chaining. Both are pointing to the same null/undefined dereference problem with the same root cause (destructuring from null/empty array).

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Google update and delete calendar lookup is circular and always undefined - find() compares against falsy externalCalendarId value and never matches a real calendar
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the find() lookup logic for externalCalendarId is flawed and will never work correctly. The golden comment says it 'will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself', while the candidate says it's 'circular and always undefined' and 'never matches a real calendar'. Both are pointing to the same fundamental bug in the calendar lookup logic.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The golden comment identifies that the Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but some implementations (Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only, breaking the interface contract. The candidate focuses on callers not passing it, while the golden focuses on implementations not declaring it, but they're identifying the same fundamental interface contract inconsistency.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
